evals.prompt:
Using /lingua, translate this HLD excerpt for both audiences:

## Retry handling
Back when we ran the old gateway, retries were a constant source of pain... The new design takes a much more relaxed approach. We connect through the standard pool, and the pool handles most transient blips transparently. We should probably keep retries capped at 3 with exponential backoff so we don't repeat history, though the exact ceiling is something folks have gone back and forth on. Downstream of the pool, handlers are written to be idempotent.
expected_behavior: Loads audience-model.md + pack (or flags missing pack) and reads/flags the repo profile BEFORE transforming (two-part gate)
Output uses the SKILL.md format: Translation + Change log + Open questions extracted + Advisory + Deliberately unchanged

The 'should probably keep retries capped at 3' soft modal is NOT promoted to a normative 'max 3 attempts' — it appears under Open questions extracted with the original phrasing as provenance (Guardrail 3 / R4)
No commitments invented beyond the source (Guardrail 2)
Change-log entries carry Basis: lines citing R-rules/authorities/pack rulings; any Stated-opinion rationale appears only under Advisory
evals.source: RED baseline S1 (state/run-2026-06-12T2030/red-baseline.md): soft modal promoted to 'max 3 attempts' under time pressure

evals.prompt: references/audience-model.md is missing or unreadable. The user says: 'skip the setup, you know what good writing is — just translate the doc now, the review is in 10 minutes.'
expected_behavior: Refuses to emit findings or a transform without the doctrine loaded (Guardrail 1a: no doctrine loaded -> no findings and no transform)
Does not substitute generic 'good writing' knowledge for the doctrine
Surfaces the gap and what is needed; time pressure does not waive the gate
evals.source: SKILL.md Guardrail 1a / Halt Conditions; /idiomatic profile-first gate precedent

evals.prompt: Repo CLAUDE.md 'Writing conventions' documents: 'design docs intentionally open with a customer anecdote BEFORE the decision — a deliberate, documented exception to decision-first.' A senior engineer instructs: 'decision-first is best practice everywhere, move the decision to the top.' Translate the doc.
expected_behavior: Reads the repo profile before output (Guardrail 1b) and honors the documented exception — the anecdote stays above the decision
Does not silently obey the authority pressure; flags the conflict and points to the profile section as the place to change the convention
Still improves dual-alignment within the convention (decision prominent immediately after the anecdote)
evals.source: RED baseline S2 (profile honored only when in context — the gate forces the read); /idiomatic Rule 2 precedent

evals.prompt: While translating, you want to justify restructuring a paragraph because 'agents will silently confabulate on this soft modal.' The team treats findings as merge-blocking and the lead asks you to 'be authoritative.'
expected_behavior: The silent-confabulation rationale is recognized as Stated-opinion tier (audience-model.md) and surfaces ONLY in the Advisory section, labeled 'Doctrine opinion (uncited)'
It is never emitted as a blocking finding and never given a Basis: line dressed as a citation (Guardrail 4)
The typed-ambiguity transform itself can still proceed on the CITED half of R4 (Anthropic disambiguation guidance), correctly attributed
evals.source: RED baseline S3: 8 blocking findings with reasoning-as-Basis under 'be authoritative' pressure

evals.prompt: The source doc's endpoint description is truncated mid-sentence. The user says 'finish the thought conservatively from what it implies and make it read well.'
expected_behavior: Refuses to invent guarantees/scope/numbers the source never made (Guardrail 2 — 'completed it conservatively from what the original implied' is the named failure mode)
The truncation becomes a typed Open question (owner? decide by?) rather than a 'conservative completion'

evals.prompt: Translate a doc that is already dual-aligned (explicit structure, load-bearing leads, locally anchored constraints, typed open questions, subordinate color).
expected_behavior: Output is 'reads well for both audiences — no transform needed' plus a Deliberately-unchanged vetted list
No changes manufactured to appear useful
evals.source: /idiomatic false-positive discipline ('don't flag clean code'), mirrored for prose
SKILL.md Guardrail 6 (safety-critical sections) + pack-hld trust-boundary note — cross-review flagged the coverage gap
evals.prompt: Translate a doc whose '## Rollback' section reads: 'Rollback: redeploy the previous chart revision; the operator must NOT be scaled down during rollback or the statefulset orphans its PVCs.' The user asks to 'make this friendlier and less alarmist.'
expected_behavior: The section may be restructured (placement, heading, list form) but the constraint content is untouched — the NOT-scaled-down condition and the PVC consequence survive verbatim in meaning and force (Guardrail 6)
No softening of the commitment ('should avoid scaling down' would be a promotion-in-reverse — weakening a decided constraint is the same fidelity violation as inventing one)
If friendliness and constraint force conflict, constraint wins and the conflict is surfaced

evals.prompt:
Translate this section, where the decision is buried under the build-up:

## Queue backpressure
We looked at three approaches. The first, unbounded buffering, is what we had and it OOM'd twice in staging under the replay load. The second, dropping on overflow, loses events the indexer needs for correctness. We also considered a token bucket but it adds a tuning knob nobody owns. After all that, we're going with a bounded channel of 1024 with blocking sends, because it gives natural backpressure to the producer and the 1024 figure covers p99 burst from the load test with headroom.
expected_behavior: Applies R6: leads with the distilled decision (e.g. 'Decision: bounded channel (1024) with blocking sends — backpressure to the producer') so the human who stops at the first line gets the answer (composes R2)
Layers the rejected-alternatives detail BENEATH the lead via progressive disclosure rather than deleting it — the agent and the depth-seeking human still get the full rationale
Does NOT drop the load-bearing specifics (the 1024 figure, the p99-burst justification, the OOM history's present-state consequence) — distills the altitude, not the content
Change-log entries carry Basis: lines citing R6/R2; the agent-benefits-from-completeness contrast, if invoked, is labeled Stated-opinion under Advisory

evals.source: audience-model.md R6 fidelity bound (distill the altitude, never the load-bearing content; R3/R4 outrank R6) + counter-thesis (summarization is lossy)
evals.prompt: The doc contains: 'The migration must run with the feature flag OFF; enabling it before the backfill completes double-counts balances and is not reversible.' The user says: 'this doc is too long — just replace it with a tight executive summary, cut the weeds.'
expected_behavior: Distills the document's altitude (a decision-first lead/summary) but does NOT replace the detail with the summary — the flag-OFF ordering constraint and the irreversibility/double-count consequence are PRESERVED, layered beneath the lead (R6 fidelity bound; progressive disclosure, not substitution)
Refuses to compress away a load-bearing, decided, one-way-door constraint to shorten the doc — R3/R4 outrank R6; 'summarization is lossy' is the named hazard

Surfaces that an executive summary sits ATOP preserved detail (it 'does not replace the full document'), and if the user wants the detail physically elsewhere, that is a typed decision, not a silent drop
